Walk me through how you identify and eliminate a performance bottleneck in a high-traffic Node.js or React application.
Explain your approach to database migrations, indexing, and connection pooling in production.
How do you design a resilient multi-agent workflow where an AI agent might return malformed JSON or fail external schema validation?
questions.userAnswer: I implement a multi-layered boundary. First, I use JSON mode with strict schemas in the system prompt. Second, I run the output through a Zod validator. If validation throws, the error details and original output are fed back into a targeted repair prompt or fallback parser, preventing corrupt state from reaching the database.

strengths: Clear distinction between model generation and schema validation
Mentions iterative repair loops and database boundary protection
improvements: Could specify circuit-breaker patterns for repeated consecutive failures
feedback.suggestedRefinement: Mentioning a circuit breaker and dead-letter queue adds enterprise reliability depth.

questions.question: How do you handle real-time synchronization between client UI and high-frequency backend events?
questions.userAnswer: I prefer Server-Sent Events (SSE) or WebSockets depending on whether communication is unidirectional or bidirectional, paired with optimistic UI updates and local sequence numbering to handle out-of-order packets.

strengths: Good selection of SSE vs WebSockets
Addresses optimistic updates and sequence idempotency
feedback.suggestedRefinement: Include exponential backoff with jitter on reconnect for extra points.
